title: THE SECURE PENDING BOX
goal: Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.

steps.action: Imagine a container whose lock, size, material, and location feel credible.
Place only what cannot be processed now inside it.
Name what is stored and when it will be revisited, ideally with support.
Close the container and reorient to the next task for today.

win: ✓ Someone else’s share moved back out of my hands.
supports: Gently exhale after “Close Container”; orient to now.
I can use “Place Cannot” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Imagine Container → Place Cannot → Name Stored → Close Container
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use containment to postpone urgent safeguarding or necessary care.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BUILD SAFE-ENOUGH, NOT PERFECT
goal: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.

steps.action: Picture a place using five sensory facts and one control feature: an exit, boundary, companion, or adjustable distance.
practise entering through a specific cue and leaving on purpose.
Strengthen the detail that produces the clearest bodily yes.

win: ✓ Progress no longer has to audition as perfection.
supports: Gently exhale after “Strengthen Safe-Enough”; orient to now.
I can use “Rehearse Specific” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Place Five → Rehearse Specific → Strengthen Safe-Enough
safety:
PAUSE
Abandon imagery that attracts threat memories or increases unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH
goal: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.

steps.action: As events arise, apply a quiet category: hearing, planning, heat, remembering, pressure.
Use one word once, then return to the raw event.
If a label starts producing analysis, name that ‘explaining’ and release it.

win: ✓ One word was enough; explanation did not get a sequel.
supports: Exhale after “Name Lightly”; keep the compass.
I can use “Use Word” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Apply Quiet → Use Word → Name Lightly
safety:
PAUSE
Drop noting if labels become compulsive, critical, or distancing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
goal: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.

steps.action: Choose an anchor and notice the precise moment contact breaks.
Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.
Track the interval between noticing and reconnection.
Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps.

win: ✓ The practice has fewer leaks than it did a minute ago.
supports: One exhale after “Let Practice”; redirect attention.
I can use “Return Instead” amid noise.
formula_flow: Choose Precise → Return Instead → Track Interval → Let Practice
safety:
PAUSE
Release focus if effort becomes rigid, painful, or compulsive.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
goal: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.

steps.action: Choose one harmless five-letter word, such as TABLE. Use each letter once; there is no need to finish perfectly.
For the first letter, name a neutral object beginning with it—T for tree, for example.
Picture that object for about two seconds with no action, meaning, memory, or story.
Jump to the next letter and a completely unrelated object. End after five letters; do not score sleep.

win: ✓ I ended after five letters; do not score sleep.
supports: Exhale after “Jump Letter”; loosen the label.
I can use “Call Object” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Pick Word → Call Object → Flash Image → Jump Letter
safety:
PAUSE
Use only while safely resting; never while driving. Stop if images become distressing, compulsive, or disorienting.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE ACTION HAD MANY AUTHORS
goal: Total doership omits most of the production team.

steps.action: Review one action and name its conditions: intention, habit, body capacity, other people, tools, timing, culture, and chance.
Place yourself among these causes rather than above them.
Keep responsibility for your contribution while releasing sole authorship.

win: ✓ Body noise no longer gets to write the conclusion alone.
supports: Gently exhale after “Keep Responsibility”; no forcing.
I can use “Place Yourself” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Name Conditions → Place Yourself → Keep Responsibility
safety:
PAUSE
Do not scattered accountability for choices that caused harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
goal: A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.

steps.action: Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, messy mental sketch, or unfinished opening.
Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly.

win: ✓ The work can move without earning a flawless score first.
supports: Exhale after “Continue Clean”; release the score.
I can use “Make Wrong” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Throwaway → Make Wrong → Fix One → Continue Clean
safety:
PAUSE
Never use deliberate errors in medical, legal, financial, safety-critical, submitted, or live shared work.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ALLY OR SABOTEUR?
goal: Judge the mental move by how it treats your life.

steps.action: Ask the current thought three questions: Does it clarify the next move?
Does it protect something real?
Does it leave me more capable afterward?
Score each yes or no.
If it fails two, thank the warning and appoint a different inner adviser.

win: ✓ Kept the warning, fired the sabotage, and chose a better adviser.
supports: Exhale after “Thank Warning”; slow the clock.
I can use “Check Protection” without rushing.
formula_flow: Ask Thought → Check Protection → Leave Me → Score Yes → Thank Warning
safety:
PAUSE
A harsh message may still contain facts; extract them before dismissal.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: STOP RENEWING THE CONSTRUCTION
goal: Some mental worlds persist through continuous subscription.

steps.action: Spot the image, conclusion, or demand being refreshed.
For one minute, refuse only the renewal: no new scene, argument, or confirmation.
Let existing residue fade at its own rate.
Redirect the freed attention into a chosen sensory task.

win: ✓ The construction crew clocked off; attention returned to the real room.
supports: I can use “Time” to return here.
formula_flow: Identify Image → Time → Let Existing → Redirect
safety:
PAUSE
Do not withdraw intention from real obligations or safety planning.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PRECISE OUTSIDE, QUIET INSIDE
goal: Action can be sharp without inner warfare.

steps.action: Set the exact external behaviour required.
Execute it with full timing and skill.
Meanwhile, decline the running argument about authorship, resentment, or imagined applause.
Allow the body act and the inner courtroom remain closed until the task ends.

win: ✓ The action stayed precise while the inner courtroom stayed closed.
supports: Gently exhale after “Let Body”; no forcing.
I can use “Execute” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Define → Execute → Imagine Applause → Let Body
safety:
PAUSE
Process emotions later if quieting argument would become suppression.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NEXT PHYSICAL MOVEMENT
goal: Projects become executable when nouns turn into verbs.

steps.action: Take the stuck item and ask what your body would visibly do first: open, call, search, carry, type, ask, measure.
Include the object and location.
do that movement before planning the remainder.

win: ✓ Planning shrank to one physical move.
supports: Gently exhale after “Plan Remainder”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Include Object” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Take Stuck → Include Object → Plan Remainder
safety:
PAUSE
Check dependencies first when the movement could create hard to undo consequences.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SOFT DELIVERY, SOLID MESSAGE
goal: Relationship care does not require surrendering the point.

steps.action: Remove attacks from your wording.
Show one sign of genuine interest, validate the understandable part of the other experience, and use an easy rather than contemptuous manner.
Keep your core message unchanged.
Gentleness edits delivery, not truth.

win: ✓ I softened the delivery without softening the message.
supports: Exhale after “Edit Delivery”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Validate Understandable” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Remove Attacks → Validate Understandable → Keep Core → Edit Delivery
safety:
PAUSE
Do not prioritise pleasantness over protection in abusive dynamics.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SELF-RESPECT CHECKSUM
goal: A conversation should not corrupt your own values.

steps.action: Before responding, verify four conditions: fair to both sides; no apology for merely existing or setting a limit; aligned with your values; completely truthful.
Revise any sentence that fails the checksum.
Then speak without extra justification.

win: ✓ Message delivered cleanly—no extra defence added.
supports: Exhale after “Speak Cleanly”; keep the compass.
I can use “Revise Sentence” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Respond Verify → Revise Sentence → Speak Cleanly
safety:
PAUSE
Fairness does not require equal power where harm or coercion exists.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: VALIDATE AT THE DEPTH YOU ACTUALLY HAVE
goal: Understanding has levels; do not counterfeit the deepest one.

steps.action: Start with attention. Reflect what you heard.
Identify the emotion if clear.
Include context that makes the response understandable.
Acknowledge valid facts.
Stop at the highest honest rung.

win: ✓ Honesty stopped at the rung it could truly reach.
supports: Exhale after “Stop Highest”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Name Emotion” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Start Attention → Name Emotion → Add Context → Acknowledge → Stop Highest
safety:
PAUSE
Validation should not endorse abuse, delusion, or dangerous conduct.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE FOUR-PART LIMIT
goal: A boundary becomes real when follow-through is inside your control.

steps.action: State the triggering condition, your limit, the action you will take, and when you will take it.
Remove threats that depend on the other person changing.
Practise the line once at speaking volume, then prepare the consequence before delivery.

win: ✓ My boundary now includes the part I can actually enforce.
supports: Exhale after “Practise Line”; release extra load.
I can use “Remove Threats” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: State Triggering → Remove Threats → Practise Line
safety:
PAUSE
Seek safety planning before setting boundaries with a violent or controlling person.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CARE WITHOUT CARRYING
goal: Empathy can cross a boundary; obligation must show its passport.

steps.action: Name the other person’s feeling and your own current feeling separately.
Locate each relative to your body.
Ask what compassionate action is actually yours and what emotional work remains theirs.
Offer the first without absorbing the second.

win: ✓ The boundary became visible without turning cold.
supports: Exhale after “Care Without Carrying”; release extra load.
I can use “Locate Relative” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Separate Feelings → Locate Relative → Ask Compassionate → Care Without Carrying
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use emotional separation to abandon genuine duty of care.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.
goal: Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.

steps.action: Imagine the person in front of you.
In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.

win: ✓ I let the message stay only in my mind.
supports: “Do Not Edit” keeps clarity above heat.
I can use “Say What Happened” without extra heat.
formula_flow: See The Person → Say What Happened → Do Not Edit → Wait
safety:
PAUSE
Stop and seek support if the exercise increases revenge thoughts, fear, or trauma.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE TWENTY-MINUTE TRUTH STORY
goal: A private story can help your mind make sense of an event.

steps.action: Choose up to twenty minutes.
In your mind, move through what occurred, what you felt, and what it means now.
End by naming your location, today’s date, and one caring action you can take.
Try again on another day only if it helps.

win: ✓ The story got a container, an ending, and permission to stay private.
supports: Exhale after “Repeat if Useful”; loosen the label.
I can use “Tell The Story” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Set A Time → Tell The Story → Return to Now → Repeat if Useful
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the story harms your sleep, safety, or daily life.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CROSS OUT THE EXPIRED FUTURE
goal: A prediction should lose influence when its decision window closes.

steps.action: Picture the prediction and the exact condition that makes it obsolete: date passed, result known, action completed, evidence changed.
When that condition arrives, imagine a line through the prediction and picture the word EXPIRED.
It may remain historically visible, but it receives no further vote.

win: ✓ The expired future lost its vote.
supports: Exhale after “Remove Vote”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Imagine Line” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Picture Prediction → Imagine Line → Remove Vote
safety:
PAUSE
Reopen only when genuinely new evidence creates a new forecast.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TURN ANTICIPATION INTO INVENTORY
goal: Body alarm earns its keep only through preparation.

steps.action: Each time the same future scene repeats, extract one actionable item: question, document, rehearsal, route, support, or if-then link.
Add it to a checklist.
When repetition yields no new preparation, stamp the simulation PAID IN FULL and switch to execution.

win: ✓ Anticipation became inventory instead of another rehearsal.
supports: Exhale after “Stamp Simulation”; then keep moving.
I can use “Add Checklist” before motivation.
formula_flow: Repeat Extract → Add Checklist → Stamp Simulation
safety:
PAUSE
Keep planning active for newly emerging risks rather than silencing them.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE LIFE RETURNED TEST
goal: Imagine receiving this ordinary day back.

steps.action: Picture having lost access to your current life and unexpectedly waking inside it again.
What small feature would suddenly matter—someone’s voice, a body ability, unfinished work, morning light?
Choose one behaviour that honours that recovered value today, without romanticising real hardship.

win: ✓ Ordinary life regained enough value to deserve one move today.
supports: Gently exhale after “Choose Behaviour”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Small” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Picture → Small → Choose Behaviour
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid loss imagery if it worsens grief, trauma, or suicidal thinking.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: A NOTE FROM TOMORROW MORNING
goal: Let the consequence-bearer make one request.

steps.action: Imagine tomorrow-you after tonight’s urge has passed. Let them ask: ‘Please protect at least…’ Then choose one minimum: sleep, money, sobriety, dignity, preparation, or safety.
Mentally sign the request with tomorrow’s date.
Bring that promise to mind exactly where the immediate choice happens.

win: ✓ Tomorrow-me got one clean favour from me today.
supports: Exhale after “Place the Contract”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Date It” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Picture Tomorrow → Date Sign → Place Contract
safety:
PAUSE
Use live support when an urge threatens serious harm or relapse.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS
goal: Language can lower heat without lowering truth.

steps.action: Underline absolutes and inflammatory terms in your account.
Exchange every one for a precise factual equivalent: ‘always’ becomes the actual frequency; ‘destroyed’ becomes the specific loss; ‘evil’ becomes the observed behaviour.
Re-read and notice what action the cooler version supports.

win: ✓ The facts stayed; the heat came down.
supports: Exhale after “Read Action”; then keep moving.
I can use “Observe Behaviour” before motivation.
formula_flow: Underline → Observe Behaviour → Read Action
safety:
PAUSE
Retain strong moral language when accurate naming is necessary.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LOOK FOR THE MISSING DANGER
goal: Absence becomes evidence only after prediction says what should be present.

steps.action: Ask what sign must exist right now if the feared model is correct.
Search once, fairly.
If it is absent, keep that absence and reduce—not erase—the model’s weight.
Name the alternate explanation strengthened by the missing sign.

win: ✓ What should have been there was missing—and that absence finally counted.
supports: Exhale after “Name Explanation”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Search Fairly” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Ask Sign → Search Fairly → Mark Absence → Name Explanation
safety:
PAUSE
Never use absent evidence to dismiss subtle or delayed safety risks.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THREE ACTIVE FUTURES ONLY
goal: Forecasts must compete for limited shelf space.

steps.action: Picture the three predictions currently most relevant.
Any new prediction may enter only by retiring one, merging with one, or proving higher usefulness for a decision.
Remove retired entries from view.
Act from the remaining portfolio rather than unlimited mental possibilities.

win: ✓ Alarm lost its 100-percent certainty.
supports: Exhale after “Act Portfolio”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Enter Retiring” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Picture Predictions → Enter Retiring → Cross Out → Act Portfolio
safety:
PAUSE
Expand the budget temporarily during genuine complex planning.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT
goal: Charge felt importance rent before it enters the decision.

steps.action: Score the information on two separate axes: how noticeable it feels and how much it changes the choice.
A dramatic item with low relevance pays a felt importance tax and moves down the priority list.
Allocate attention to decision impact instead.

win: ✓ Made vividness pay rent before it could buy my attention.
supports: Exhale after “Allocate Attention”; notice the room.
I can use “Pay Felt” to return here.
formula_flow: Score Information → Pay Felt → Allocate Attention
safety:
PAUSE
High-felt importance warnings still deserve review when safety is plausible.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
goal: Useful reflection needs a finish signal physiology can recognise.

steps.action: Choose one finish you can repeat: wash your hands, hear a soft sound, touch a doorframe, or change the light.
Pair it with one short answer in your mind and a time to think about it again.
Use the sensory finish only when the topic is truly closed.

win: ✓ The topic got a sensory full stop instead of another mental reopening.
supports: Exhale after “Close It”; notice the room.
“Choose A Finish” to “Close It”: what loosened?
I can use “Pair It” to return here.
formula_flow: Choose A Finish → Pair It → Close It
safety:
PAUSE
Do not close matters that still require urgent action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MEASURE THE EMOTION’S VELOCITY
goal: Intensity is a photograph; momentum is the film.

steps.action: At three intervals, keep not only level but direction and speed: rising fast, steady, falling slowly.
Add the action impulse at each point.
Make decisions from trajectory plus facts, not from the first intensity number alone.

win: ✓ The feeling became a moving trend, not a frozen number.
supports: Exhale after “Make Decisions”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Add Action” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Set Level → Add Action → Make Decisions
safety:
PAUSE
Escalating risk calls for support before further tracking.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN EACH LOAD TO ITS SOURCE
goal: One problem should not carry the weight of the whole week.

steps.action: Name current stressors and estimate each contribution to body alarm.
Imagine arrows from the present feeling back to its actual sources.
Address the largest actionable contributor first; stop blaming the most visible issue for unrelated load.

win: ✓ The week stopped collapsing into one overloaded problem.
supports: Exhale after “Stop Blaming”; then keep moving.
I can use “Imagine Arrows” before motivation.
formula_flow: Estimate Contribution → Imagine Arrows → Stop Blaming
safety:
PAUSE
Keep estimates temporary when sources are unclear.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE THE RHYTHM, CHANGE THE STATE
goal: Emotion maintains itself through tempo as well as story.

steps.action: Notice the cadence of speech, movement, or breathing.
Choose an opposite rhythm: agitated becomes deliberate, collapsed becomes lightly brisk, looping becomes irregular.
Maintain the new tempo through one simple task and observe the emotional shift.

win: ✓ I changed the tempo and gave the state a different rhythm to follow.
supports: Gently exhale after “Observe Emotional”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Choose Opposite” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Cadence → Choose Opposite → Observe Emotional
safety:
PAUSE
Match movement to medical ability and avoid breath manipulation if activating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GLOBAL LABELS NEED THREE RECEIPTS
goal: Identity claims must show recent action evidence.

steps.action: When ‘I’m lazy,’ ‘I’m unlovable,’ or another global Name appears, demand three specific behaviours from the last month that support it and three that complicate it.
If the evidence is mixed, replace identity with a narrower situational description.

win: ✓ The global label could not produce three clean receipts.
supports: Exhale after “Replace Identity”; loosen the label.
I can use “Replace Identity” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Name Appears → Replace Identity
safety:
PAUSE
Do not turn the audit into exhaustive self-surveillance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TRAIT OR OLD PROTECTION STRATEGY?
goal: Personality may be a solution that outlived its original problem.

steps.action: Choose the disliked trait.
Ask what threat it once reduced and what payoff maintains it now.
Design one alternative strategy that offers the same protection with lower cost.
Test it in a low-stakes situation before rewriting identity.

win: ✓ My worth and their reaction are separate again.
supports: Exhale after “Test Low”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Ask Threat” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Choose Disliked → Ask Threat → Design Alternative → Test Low
safety:
PAUSE
Do not pathologise temperament or neurodivergence to force conformity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE
goal: Pain may be stored without its later survival chapter.

steps.action: Retell only enough to reach the painful ending.
Then append what actually followed: escape, help, adaptation, learning, regained ability, or today’s status.
Do not invent redemption.
Restore the omitted chronology.

win: ✓ I restored the survival chapter the painful memory had cut off.
supports: I can use “Follow Escape” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: End Retell → Follow Escape → Don't Invent → Restore
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid forced positive meaning where aftermath remains unresolved.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SAY THE SENTENCE HISTORY NEVER RECEIVED
goal: Symbolic completion can end a language loop without rewriting facts.

steps.action: Picture the exact words you could not say or hear.
Say them quietly in your mind or to an empty room while clearly stating that this is present-day completion, not a changed past.
Add the response current-you can now provide.

win: ✓ The mental rerun has an exit now.
supports: Exhale after “Add Response”; end the lap.
I can use “Speak Empty” without another lap.
formula_flow: Picture Words → Speak Empty → Add Response
safety:
PAUSE
Do not contact unsafe people or mistake imagined response for evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
goal: When the doorway is the problem, let chance choose a safe entrance.

steps.action: Name three to six task sections that can safely be done in any order and give each one a number.
Use a random-number tool on your phone to choose one number. Do not pick again just because you dislike the number.
Work only inside that section for ninety seconds; do not reorganise the whole project.
Notice one concrete sign of progress, then decide whether to choose another number or close.

win: ✓ A random door beat the perfect doorway.
supports: Exhale after “Mark Progress”; release extra blame.
I can use “Let Chance Choose” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Number Doors → Let Chance Choose → Enter There → Mark Progress
safety:
PAUSE
Use this only for reorderable work; never randomise required safety, medical, legal, financial, or technical sequences.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SET UP WHILE ENERGY IS CHEAP
goal: Tomorrow’s low-motivation self should inherit a nearly finished start.

steps.action: During a higher-energy window, prepare every requirement: pack, remember in, charge, open, measure, place, or prefill.
Leave only the final movement for the difficult time.
Photograph or Notice the ready state.

win: ✓ Low-energy me inherited a start that was already waiting.
supports: Exhale after “Leave It Ready”; release extra blame.
I can use “Leave Final” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Prepare Requirement → Leave Final → Leave It Ready
safety:
PAUSE
Keep sensitive accounts, medication, food, and equipment securely prepared.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LEAVE A BRIDGE BACK
goal: A break should not erase the state needed to restart.

steps.action: Before stopping, picture the precise next movement, current reasoning, and any open file or tool.
Leave the workspace at a deliberate re-entry point.
On return, follow the Notice before reviewing the whole project.

win: ✓ I left myself a bridge back instead of a blank restart.
supports: Exhale after “Return Reviewing”; release extra blame.
I can use “Leave Workspace” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Stop Precise → Leave Workspace → Return Reviewing
safety:
PAUSE
Update the bridge when conditions or priorities change.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ENTER THROUGH THE SIDE DOOR
goal: Resistance may accept a neighbouring move.

steps.action: Pick a small action beside the main task: open one file before starting the work, put on walking shoes before deciding to walk, or wash one ingredient before cooking.
Start with that small step and let it naturally lead into the main task.

win: ✓ Accountability stayed; self-punishment lost ground.
supports: Exhale after “Let It Lead”; release extra blame.
“Choose Side Door” keeps blame in proportion.
“Choose Side Door” → “Let It Lead”: what changed?
I can use “Let It Lead” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Choose Side Door → Let It Lead
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid decoys that become elaborate avoidance rituals.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT THE FIRST OBJECT IN THE PATH
goal: Let the space issue a clear instruction.

steps.action: Spot the first object the desired behaviour requires.
Position it where normal movement will encounter it at the right time.
Remove competing cues from that path.
When you meet the object, do the linked first action before walking past.

win: ✓ The first object in the path gave the first instruction.
supports: Exhale after “Meet the Cue”; release extra blame.
I can use “Position” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Identify Object → Position → Remove Competing → Meet the Cue
safety:
PAUSE
Never create trip hazards, privacy breaches, or unsafe access.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAP THE RELATIONSHIP LABOUR
goal: Imbalance becomes negotiable after it becomes visible.

steps.action: Across a defined period, tally who initiates, accommodates, repairs, plans, and carries emotional follow-up.
Include background for genuine capacity differences.
Discuss the pattern using categories, not accusations, and request one clear rebalance.

win: ✓ The invisible relationship labour became visible enough to negotiate.
supports: Exhale after “Use Categories”; keep both sides.
I can use “Add Context” before concluding.
formula_flow: Plan Carries → Add Context → Use Categories
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use the map to demand identical contributions under unequal circumstances.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
goal: Choose the mistake you can catch early enough to fix.

steps.action: Name the two or three live options. For each, picture the specific way it could fail—not a vague fear.
Name the earliest visible sign that failure has begun. It must be visible or clear, not a feeling alone.
State what corrective action would still be available when that sign appears and what cost has already accumulated.
Choose the option whose reliable warning arrives while correction is still practical. Use this as one decision criterion, not the whole verdict.

win: ✓ The decision stopped needing one perfect criterion.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Visible”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Name Failure” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Name Options → Name Failure → Warning → Choose Visible
safety:
PAUSE
For high-stakes, irreversible, medical, legal, financial, or safety decisions, use qualified advice and all required criteria.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND THE MOMENT THE FLOOR CATCHES YOU
goal: Panic can obscure support that never disappeared.

steps.action: Stand safely and shift weight slowly left, centre, right, then forward and back.
At each transition, spot the exact instant the receiving foot supports you.
Finish at centre and name the strongest contact point.

win: ✓ The nervous system fired; choice stayed available.
supports: Exhale after “Finish Centre”; then keep moving.
I can use “Identify Instant” before motivation.
formula_flow: Shift Weight → Identify Instant → Finish Centre
safety:
PAUSE
Practise seated or with assistance if balance is uncertain.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BORROW STILLNESS FROM THE WALL
goal: Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.

steps.action: Rest your gaze on a stable line, corner, or heavy object.
Compare its visual constancy with the motion inside your body and mind.
Do not make the inner movement match.
Let both facts coexist until the outer reference becomes usable.

win: ✓ Stillness entered the scene, so movement stopped being the whole field.
supports: Exhale after “Let Facts”; notice the room.
I can use “Compare Visual” to return here.
formula_flow: Rest Gaze → Compare Visual → Don't Match → Let Facts
safety:
PAUSE
Do not stare at one point when operating a vehicle or feeling dizzy.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
goal: Urgency shrinks when hearing regains depth.

steps.action: Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer.
Move attention outward through those distances, then back once.
Let the far sound widen the perceived space around the closest one.

win: ✓ Distance came back into hearing, and urgency got smaller.
supports: Exhale after “Let Far”; slow the clock.
I can use “Move Attention” without rushing.
formula_flow: Identify Nearest → Move Attention → Let Far
safety:
PAUSE
Use hearing protection rather than attention practice in unsafe noise.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GIVE THE FINGERS A HARDER PROBLEM
goal: Complex texture can interrupt low-information mental repetition.

steps.action: Find a safe textured object.
Explore ridges, grain, temperature, resistance, transitions, and imbalance with precise fingertips.
Name details that require fresh sensory discrimination.
Continue until the description can no longer be generated automatically.

win: ✓ Repetition lost traction when the fingers demanded real detail.
supports: Exhale after “Continue Description”; end the lap.
I can use “Explore” without another lap.
formula_flow: Find Safe → Explore → Name Details → Continue Description
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid sharp, contaminated, allergenic, or painful materials.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND THE SENSE FACT THE STORY CANNOT EXPLAIN
goal: Threat models dislike contradictory present data.

steps.action: State the feared scenario.
Search for one sensory fact opposite with it: an unlocked exit, ordinary background conversation, relaxed posture nearby, intact support, current silence.
Explain in one line why the model fails to predict that fact.

win: ✓ I found a present fact the threat story could not explain away.
supports: Exhale after “Predict Fact”; keep both sides.
I can use “Search Sensory” before concluding.
formula_flow: State Fear → Search Sensory → Predict Fact
safety:
PAUSE
Never let one neutral cue overrule concrete evidence of danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: HIDE THE OPTION NAMES
goal: See what the options look like before their names start campaigning.

steps.action: Ask someone—or a shuffled note—to rename the leading options A, B and C without showing which is which.
Choose three relevant traits, such as cost, time, fit, reliability, or learning. Keep safety facts visible.
Compare the symbols on those traits without guessing their identities and hold the current order.
Reveal the names. Keep the blind order or name exactly what changed it and why.

win: ✓ The options lost their campaign slogans; the traits made the first vote.
supports: Exhale after “Reveal Options”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Choose Traits” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Mask Names → Choose Traits → Rank Blind → Reveal Options
safety:
PAUSE
Never hide facts required for safety, consent, ethics, affordability, or professional decision support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CLOSE THE INPUT VALVE
goal: Consolidation cannot occur during endless intake.

steps.action: Choose a defined period with no nonessential news, feeds, podcasts, searches, or advice.
Keep a Notice for impulses to consume.
Observe what memories, conclusions, or next actions emerge when fresh input stops.

win: ✓ Once input stopped, the mind finally had room to consolidate.
supports: Exhale after “Observe Memories”; mark the pause.
I can use “Keep Impulses” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Choose Defined → Keep Impulses → Observe Memories
safety:
PAUSE
Maintain essential communication and emergency alerts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GROUP BY BRAIN MODE
goal: Context switching charges a restart fee.

steps.action: Group tasks into simple types such as talking, reading, errands, decisions, or admin.
Put tasks that use the identical kind of attention together.
Complete that block before changing to a different kind of task.

win: ✓ The old sequence no longer owns the next move.
supports: Exhale after “Finish The Block”; mark the pause.
“Make One Block” proves choice interrupted habit.
What lost power: “Sort by Mode” → “Finish The Block”?
I can use “Make One Block” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Sort by Mode → Make One Block → Finish The Block
safety:
PAUSE
Keep flexibility for urgent interruptions and fatigue.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHEN DOES THIS INFORMATION EXPIRE?
goal: Data should not remain active after its conditions disappear.

steps.action: For each influential input, picture an expiry condition: price changes, role ends, policy updates, health status shifts, deadline passes.
Notice any expired item. Stop letting it guide new behaviour until the information is refreshed.

win: ✓ Expired information lost its voting rights until it earns an update.
supports: Exhale after “Expire Old Data”; mark the pause.
“Picture Expiry” to “Expire Old Data”: what loosened?
I can use “Expire Old Data” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Picture Expiry → Expire Old Data
safety:
PAUSE
Preserve historical records even after action expiry.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE BEFORE MOTIVATION
goal: Feeling ready is not a legal requirement for the first motion.

steps.action: State honestly: ‘Motivation may stay absent.’ Begin the earliest physical component anyway—stand, open, carry, type, dial.
Continue only through one contained unit.
Let action provide data about if further movement is available.

win: ✓ Action produced data before motivation arrived.
supports: Exhale after “Test Momentum”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Complete Unit” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Begin Anyway → Complete Unit → Test Momentum
safety:
PAUSE
Rest rather than override illness, burnout, or genuine incapacity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT KIND OF EFFORT IS THIS?
goal: Difficulty can signal growth, danger, novelty, or bad design.

steps.action: Classify the strain using evidence.
If danger, stop; if novelty, allow learning; if skill growth, dose it; if poor design, simplify the system.
Respond to the category instead of interpreting all effort as failure.

win: ✓ I identified what kind of effort this was before deciding what it meant.
supports: Exhale after “Respond Category”; watch the thought.
I can use “Stop Novelty” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Use Evidence → Stop Novelty → Respond Category
safety:
PAUSE
Persistent pain, exhaustion, or mental change needs professional assessment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SWAP OUTCOME CONTROL FOR PROCESS CONTROL
goal: Measure what your hands can actually influence.

steps.action: Name the desired outcome and cross it out as the score.
Substitute one visible process variable fully under your control—calls made, honest minutes practised, applications sent, boundary delivered.
Check success only on that variable for the chosen period.

win: ✓ Success moved onto the part my hands can actually control.
supports: Exhale after “Score the Process”; leave it unanswered.
“Score the Process”: what changed from “Name Desired”?
I can use “Practise Applications” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Name Desired → Practise Applications → Score the Process
safety:
PAUSE
Outcome feedback still matters for changing an ineffective process.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THREE INCOMPATIBLE READINGS
goal: Uncertainty is not evidence for your favourite meaning.

steps.action: Hold the same cue—a delayed reply, expression, result.
Generate three explanations that cannot all be true and spot what future evidence would discriminate among them.
Delay commitment until one prediction receives support.

win: ✓ Three readings stayed alive until reality started eliminating them.
supports: Exhale after “Receive Support”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Identify Future” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Hold Cue → Identify Future → Receive Support
safety:
PAUSE
Choose protective action when uncertainty itself carries unacceptable risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LEAVE ONE THING BETTER
goal: Legacy can fit inside an ordinary afternoon.

steps.action: Choose a person, place, system, or object you can improve slightly: teach one thing, repair one item, reduce one burden, plant, clean, document, encourage.
Complete the act without needing it to prove anything about you.

win: ✓ One thing is better now. No grand meaning required.
supports: Exhale after “Leave It Better”; keep both sides.
I can use “Leave It Better” before concluding.
formula_flow: Choose Person → Leave It Better
safety:
PAUSE
Do not overextend yourself in the name of legacy.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SOFTEN BOTH SIDES OF SEEING
goal: Perceiver and perceived need not stay rigidly opposed.

steps.action: Choose a simple object or sound.
Attend at the shared time to its qualities and the act of perceiving.
Refuse to place all reality on either side.
Let the relationship event—seeing or hearing—become primary for several seconds.

win: ✓ Seeing became a relationship, not a rigid split.
supports: Exhale after “Let Relationship”; watch the thought.
I can use “Attend Time” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Choose Simple → Attend Time → Place Reality → Let Relationship
safety:
PAUSE
Keep ordinary boundaries clear in social, legal, and safety contexts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT MATERIAL CONSEQUENCE DOES STATUS ACTUALLY HAVE?
goal: Rank signals can feel like survival events long after they stop being one.

steps.action: Say the status loss without prestige language.
Name actual effects on income, access, authority, relationship, and safety.
Separate those from embarrassment or comparison.
Respond proportionately to the material column.

win: ✓ I separated the material consequence from the status sting.
supports: Exhale after “Respond Proportionately”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Name” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Describe Status → Name → Separate Embarrassment → Respond Proportionately
safety:
PAUSE
Take real discrimination, exclusion, or job risk seriously.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
